description.value: The study examined amygdala activation and functional connectivity during fearful and neutral face processing in civilian African-American women with PTSD and traumatized controls.

spans.text: Participants viewed fearful and neutral face stimuli during functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI).

value: We hypothesized that PTSD would be associated with an increased amygdala response, and with decreased functional connectivity between the amygdala and vmPFC/ACC, in response to fearful stimuli.

spans.text: We hypothesized that PTSD would be associated with an increased amygdala response, and with decreased functional connectivity between the amygdala and vmPFC/ACC, in response to fearful stimuli.

description.value: Forty African-American women with civilian trauma, including 20 with PTSD and 20 traumatized controls, participated in a cross-sectional between-group study. Participants were unmedicated and underwent fMRI while passively viewing fearful and neutral faces.
